Excel

Percentage change without the confusion.

Understand the difference between percentage change and percentage-point change before presenting the result.

TechShift Digital · Practical guide

Two questions, two different answers

If a rate rises from 20% to 25%, the increase is 5 percentage points. Relative to the original 20%, it is a 25% increase. Both statements can be correct, but they describe different comparisons.

Use the right formula

For percentage change between ordinary values, use =(B2-A2)/A2 and format the result as a percentage. Moving from 80 to 100 produces 25%.

For a percentage-point difference, subtract the two rates. If cells contain 20% and 25%, =B2-A2 returns 5% as a cell value, which you should describe as 5 percentage points.

Watch the baseline

A zero baseline has no defined percentage change. A negative baseline requires careful interpretation. Do not hide those cases behind a formula that silently replaces an error with zero.

Label the result clearly

Show the original value, new value, period and unit. Use “percentage points” when comparing rates directly, and “percentage increase” when describing relative growth.
